$schema_note: Structural map of the moria8 codebase, generated by static inspection of the source tree. Line/byte figures are point-in-time measurements, not build outputs; re-derive from source and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for authoritative current figures.

project.name: moria8
project.description: A from-scratch 6502 assembly port of the Moria roguelike, targeting Commodore 8-bit machines and the Apple IIe, sharing one platform-agnostic game core across all ports.

repository_layout.role: Platform-agnostic gameplay, UI, data, and shared logic. No hardware registers allowed here.
Contract-only Commodore HAL: lifecycle, memory, IRQ, layout, screen, input, sound, storage, overlay, entropy interfaces.
Shared Commodore implementation code: MMU macros, overlay loader, disk swap, REU, save-slot policy, title screen.
C64 entry point, platform code, HAL implementation, tests, harness scripts.
C128 entry point, boot, VDC/MMU, dual-bank runtime, tests, harness scripts.
Plus/4 entry point, TED platform code, HAL implementation, tests.
Apple IIe port: ProDOS MLI storage, aux-memory bank access, HAL implementation, boot stub, MAME harness.
Cross-architecture helper logic usable by any platform, promoted out of platforms/commodore/common.
Source data consumed by build-time generators.

Python build tooling: HAL boundary/export checkers, disk image builders (diskart, ProDOS, AppleCommander), Huffman/string-bank encoders, creature-data parser, lint checks. Third-party tools (kickass, applecommander, prodos) auto-download here at build time.
Architecture, contract, and process documentation (see docs_index).
Generated binaries, disk images, symbols, snapshots, test scratch output. Not source of truth.
Thin root wrapper dispatching to platforms/commodore and platforms/apple2 sub-makefiles.

c64_import_cascade.note: Order of #import in platforms/commodore/c64/main.s; approximates the dependency/link order and is representative of the shape all ports follow (platform HAL/services first, then core in dependency order, then platform disk/save glue, then game_loop).

hal_contract.principle: Contract-only directory: platform-specific register writes, banking mechanics, KERNAL wrappers, and drive behavior must live under the owning platform, not here.

modules.name: hal_storage.s
modules.purpose: Disk/save I/O contract, phase-banded status codes

hal_contract.apple2_note: platforms/apple2/hal/ implements the same contract surface (hal_contract.s, lifecycle_policy.s, layout.s, storage_policy.s, entropy_consts.s, memory_bank_consts.s) against ProDOS MLI and IIe aux-memory banking instead of KERNAL/IEC.

invariants: All map access goes through MapRead_*/MapWrite_* macros (25 files); only core/dungeon_data.s row tables touch MAP_BASE arithmetically.
core/rng.s reads entropy via 4 lda absolute of hal_entropy_timer* labels supplied by the platform.
Arithmetic uses core/math.s helpers; randomness uses core/rng.s, never ad hoc.
No hardware registers may appear in core/.

c128.video_audio: VDC (physical access via HAL only) / SID
c128.memory_model: Dual-bank: Bank 0 execution + scoped Bank 1 data/cache access; explicit runtime-loaded payloads
c128.source_of_truth: platforms/commodore/c128/memory128.s (ownership constants, overlap asserts); platforms/commodore/c128/main.s (segment defs, Bank 0 asserts)

plus4.video_audio: TED (owns screen, color/attribute, sound, ROM/RAM switching)
plus4.memory_model: Disk-bound 64KB like C64, but TED low-memory screen/attribute ownership shifts the main-map window
plus4.constraint: Must not leak C64 VIC-II/SID/CIA/REU/$01-banking assumptions into Plus/4 code

apple2.cpu: Apple IIe 128K, plain NMOS 6502 opcodes only (must also run on enhanced IIe/IIc)
apple2.display: 80-column text gameplay, reusing C128 layout values
apple2.memory_model: 128K main/aux split: resident $0A00-$7BFF, play slot $7C00-$9FFF, overlay window $A400-$B9FF; aux RAM holds the live map, auxdata tables, and a hot overlay cache
apple2.toolchain: Kick Assembler retained; MAME apple2ee for headless test harness; AppleCommander (auto-downloaded) builds .po disk images; ProDOS 2.4.3 kernel and boot blocks auto-download (SHA256-pinned) into tools/prodos, PRODOS/BOOTBLOCKS env overrides supported
apple2.process_rule: Full parity, hardest-problem-first, modeled on the Plus/4 port. No vertical slices, scaffolding, stubs-to-be-replaced, feature-gating defines, or probe-only builds.

c64.note: Verified against a fresh `make build64` (0/260 asserts failed): the Default segment actually links to $080e-$c162, ~354 bytes past MAP_BASE ($C000). This is intentional, not a boundary bug. main.s:1965 places `program_end:` (linked at $bfbd) as the true resident/forever boundary, asserted `<= MAP_BASE`; code emitted after that label (REU/Ultimate/turbo detection, banked-runtime loader) is explicitly commented 'Init-only code ... runs once at startup before dungeon map ... are used. Overwritten during normal gameplay.' AGENTS.md's 'must end below $C000' is the simplified restatement of intent; the enforced contract is narrower (forever-resident code + map/earthquake scratch must precede program_end, and program_end <= MAP_BASE) and deliberately permits this dead-by-runtime overlap, mirroring the C128 128.persist/128.play mutual-exclusion pattern. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's cited end address ($C129) is ~33 bytes stale relative to the current tree — cosmetic drift, not structural.

regions.owner: Forever-resident code/data (BASIC stub + machine code up to program_end; asserted <= MAP_BASE)
Init-only startup code (REU/Ultimate/turbo detection, banked-runtime loader) — deliberately overlaps MAP_BASE; dead before the map is first written, then overwritten by it
Banked runtime payload (64.bank), below CPU vectors
TED-owned (platform HAL), not the C64 VIC-II/CIA/SID model
Scratch/test/BFS path area; VDC renderer row buffers at $0500-$05ED
MMU helper blob in common RAM
Main program image: boot path, loaders, trampolines, wrappers
128.world resident world payload (cache/overlay state, filename tables, infravision helpers)
128.play gameplay payload (when loaded) - mutually exclusive with 128.persist
I/O hole; forbidden for ordinary runtime payloads
Reloadable banked runtime payload, asserted below $FF00

apple2_main.note: Verified against platforms/apple2/memory.s constants and docs/APPLE2_MEMORY_POLICY.md; MORIA8.SYSTEM boots at $2000 then relocates into the $0800-$09FF loader scratch inside the resident span.

regions.owner: Zero page: core $02-$8F unchanged; platform $90-$EF; $F0-$FF reserved
Platform scratch: ZP save buffer, MLI param blocks, boot loader staging
Overlay/tier window: one of 11 mutually-exclusive code overlays or a MONSTER.DB tier blob
Window tail reserved; tier data may use through $BAFF
ProDOS MLI I/O/staging buffer (page-aligned, one open file)

apple2_aux.note: Aux (64K bank) ownership; all aux access goes through the ZP AuxRead/AuxWrite and MapRead/MapWrite thunks.

regions.owner: A2.AUXDATA: Huffman data, item-name streams, store data, recall arrays, class-spell tables, spell names, ego suffixes, externalized strings, char-map table
Hot overlay cache (page-rounded slots): TOWN $5700, UI $6C00, SPELL $7900, MODAL $8D00, GEN $9900, ITEMS $AA00
Reserved future map span / live dungeon-town map ownership
Bank 1 DB/data region (includes 128.names item-name tokens at $7400-$7734)
Top common RAM shared with Bank 0; not cache-safe

overlay_segments_c64.note: not an $e000 overlay slot; resident banked runtime

build_system.assembler: Kick Assembler (downloads to tools/kickass/ unless KICKASS override given)
build_system.apple2_tooling: AppleCommander 13.2 auto-downloads (SHA256-pinned) to tools/applecommander; ProDOS 2.4.3 kernel + boot blocks auto-download (SHA256-pinned from ProDOS-8/ProDOS8-Releases) to tools/prodos; PRODOS/BOOTBLOCKS env overrides supported
build_system.test_runner: VICE headless (x64sc/x128/xplus4) via localhost monitor automation; MAME apple2ee for Apple IIe

root_makefile_targets.disk: builds shipping disk images for all 4 ports

build_system.verification_note: VICE/MAME-launching commands require escalated permissions on first attempt (sandbox blocks local monitor/socket access); build-only and static-check commands stay sandboxed.

Third-party: prodos/ (ProDOS 2.4.3 kernel + boot blocks, auto-downloaded, SHA256-pinned)
